name: Salt — Coarse Kosher
use_case: Chladni plates, visible demonstration (larger particles than sand)

behavior.mechanism: At the boundary between antinode (high vibration) and node (still), the net time-averaged radiation pressure force on a granule is directed toward the node. For salt, the cubic shape creates rolling friction different from spherical sand.
behavior.pattern_clarity: excellent at 50–400 Hz; too coarse above 800 Hz
behavior.special_note: Salt is hygroscopic — humidity above 75% causes the crystals to stick together, creating bridges across nodal lines that preserve the last-seen pattern even after the sound stops. This 'acoustic fossil' effect is visible for hours in humid conditions.

notes: The cubic particle shape creates sharper nodal line edges than spherical sand, because the crystals stack against each other cleanly at the node boundary. Use table salt for fine detail; kosher salt for visibility in demonstrations. Avoid fine-ground iodised salt — the iodine additive increases clumping.

demonstration_notes.cleanup: Vacuum; salt is non-hazardous and biodegradable
demonstration_notes.fire_caution: Salt on a brass plate heated by a speaker coil can cause corrosion; keep drive amplitudes below plate-warming threshold
